HELP.CONTENT_GETTING_STARTED:
This site decides which Pokémon GO alerts the Poracle bot sends you as direct messages: the Pokémon, raids, quests and other events you care about, and where they have to happen. You only hear about what you ask for.

ℹ️
Register with the bot first. Sign up with the Poracle bot on Discord or Telegram, then come back here and sign in.

Signing in

  • For Discord, press Sign in with Discord, approve the app on Discord, and you come straight back here.
  • For Telegram, if this site offers it, use the Telegram button and confirm the login in your Telegram app.
  • If your community runs its own sign-in, a third button carries its name and works the same way.

If the site has a registration page, the login page also shows a Sign up button that leads there.

First-time setup

The first time you sign in, a welcome wizard on the Dashboard walks you through three steps: set your pin, the point distances are measured from; choose the areas you want alerts from; and add your first alarm. A step for something your site has switched off is left out.

You can skip any step and do it later. The wizard stops appearing once you finish it or press Skip setup.
HELP.CONTENT_DASHBOARD:
The Dashboard is where you land after signing in. It answers one question: what will reach you right now?

The status strip

The strip along the top shows your active profile, whether your alerts are on or paused, your pin and your areas. Click the profile to switch to another one (with only one profile it opens Profiles), the pin to set or move it, and the areas to open Areas & places.

While something is quiet, a Quiet item joins the strip, saying how many and when the next one ends. Click it to see them all and start those alerts again. See Quiet periods.

Once you have a pin, the strip also shows the in-game weather there, the types it boosts and when it was last updated.

Area coverage

With areas selected, a map draws them together and names each one underneath, with its weather. An area that's quiet shows how long it has left. Click the map to open Areas & places.

Your alarms

Every alarm type you track is listed with how many alarms you have. Click one to open its list. Types with no alarms share one Not tracking line underneath. Cleaning beside the heading opens the clean mode page.

New alarm

New alarm at the top of the page lists the alarm types your site offers. Pick one and its list opens with the add dialog ready. A type your site has switched off isn't listed.

Tips

While your setup is incomplete (no pin, no areas, no alarms) a tip says so, with a button that fixes it. Dismiss the ones you don't need.

Getting around

The sidebar lists the alarm types first, then your settings: Profiles, Areas & places, My geofences and Cleaning. Help sits below them. Admins and webhook delegates get an extra group further down. On a tablet or phone the sidebar stays hidden until you press the menu button at the top left, and then opens over the page.
HELP.CONTENT_LOCATION:
Your pin is the point your alerts measure from. An alarm that reaches you within a radius uses your pin, unless you aim that alarm at a saved place instead.

Setting your pin

Click Pin in the Dashboard's status strip. On Areas & places, open Pin and places under the map and press Change, or Set if you have no pin yet. Then use whichever of these suits you:

  • Type an address, town or landmark into the search box and pick one of the suggestions. When nothing matches, the list says so; try a fuller address or a nearby town.
  • Type the latitude and longitude yourself. A value out of range is flagged straight away, and Save stays off until it's fixed.
  • Press Use my location to use your device's position. Your browser asks for permission first.
  • Click the map to put the pin there.

No search box means your admin has switched address search off. The other three still work.

Every map click and GPS fix looks the address up, so the dialog shows where the pin will land before you press Save.

The same dialog opens when you add a place or pick a one-off point for a single alarm. It's then titled Pick a point and you confirm with Use this point, which leaves your pin where it was.

💡
Want area alerts only? Clear beside your pin in Pin and places removes it. You're asked first, and the question says how many alarms measure their radius from your pin. They stop matching until you set a pin again.
HELP.CONTENT_AREAS:
Areas are zones your community has drawn on the map. The ones you select are what an alarm follows when it's set to Anywhere in my areas.

Selecting areas

Open Areas & places from the sidebar. The page opens on the map: click an area to select it and click it again to drop it. A selected area fills green with a solid outline; the rest show as a grey dashed outline. Hover over an area to see its name. Your selected areas are listed as chips under the map, and the cross on a chip drops that area.

The bar above the map switches between Map and List, says how many areas are active (saved, not just ticked) and offers Clear all. In List view, tick areas in a list you can search.

Changes aren't saved until you press Save on the bar at the bottom of the page, which says how many areas you'll have. Cancel puts your selection back as it was. If Poracle has no area by one of the names you saved, it's left out and the message after saving names it.

Regions

In List view, pick a region from the region box to narrow the list to it. Select all and Deselect all act only on what the filter has left on screen, which is how you take a whole region on or off at once. On the map, Jump to region moves the map instead of filtering anything.

Overlapping areas

A smaller area always sits on top of a larger one, so both can be clicked. Zoom in if the small one is hard to hit.

Pin and places

The map shows your pin too, and each saved place as a labelled violet dot. Both are managed in the Pin and places panel under the chips. Its header says whether your pin is set and how many places you have, and clicking a marker on the map opens it. Setting your pin covers the pin itself.

A place is a named point (work, the park you raid at, your parents' house) that an alarm can measure its radius from instead of your pin. Add one with Add a place in the panel, then pick it under Measured from when you set an alarm's delivery. A name can be up to 64 characters and can't repeat one you already have.

The move button on a place puts it on a new point and keeps its name, so every alarm measuring from it moves with it. The bin first checks whether any alarm is aimed at the place. If none is, you confirm and it's deleted. If some are, a dialog lists them and the place stays; point those alarms somewhere else first.

ℹ️
Areas belong to a profile. Each profile keeps its own selection, so switching profile shows a different set. Geofences you drew are switched on or off per profile from My geofences.
ℹ️
Not every area is listed. Admins can take an area off the list, usually a test or staging zone. If one you had selected is no longer in the list, its alerts keep coming and saving this page keeps it. It still shows among your selected areas under the map; remove it there and save if you don't want it.
HELP.CONTENT_GEOFENCES:
When none of your community's areas fits the ground you care about, draw your own.

Drawing a geofence

  1. Open My geofences from the sidebar.
  2. Press Draw geofence.
  3. Click the map to place the corners of your shape, then click the first point again to close it. It needs at least 3 points.
  4. Name it. A region is filled in when one can be detected; it only matters if an admin later makes your geofence public, so you can leave it empty.
  5. Save.

A new geofence is switched on for the profile you're using. If that step fails you'll see "Saved, but it couldn't be switched on yet. Use the toggle to retry." The geofence is saved; flip its toggle to switch it on.

Switching it on per profile

Each geofence has a toggle reading Active or Inactive for your current profile. On another profile it starts inactive; switch it on there to get its alerts on that profile too. Nothing is redrawn or copied.

ℹ️
An approved geofence has become a public area and has no toggle here. Select it on the Areas & places page like any other area.

Renaming and deleting

The pencil renames a geofence or changes its region. It's there while the geofence is private or was rejected. If a rename fails, nothing was changed and you can try again.

The bin deletes a geofence and takes it off every profile. It's hidden while a geofence waits for review and once it's approved. If some of your alarms are limited to that geofence, you're asked what happens to them: Delete those alarms too (the default) removes them on every profile, and Keep them, using my profile's areas keeps them, following each profile's areas instead.

Using a geofence for one alarm

Your geofences also appear, marked with a draw icon, in the Only in specific areas list of an alarm's delivery settings. That limits one alarm to the geofence without switching it on for the whole profile.

GeoJSON import and export

Export and Import at the top of the page move geofences in and out as GeoJSON, so you can draw a shape in a tool such as geojson.io and bring it here, or keep a copy of what you have.

Export: tick the geofences you want and you get a geofences.geojson file with one polygon each, carrying its name and region.

Import: drop a .geojson or .json file on the drop zone, or click it to browse. The file is read in your browser and every shape it holds is listed before anything is saved. Untick what you don't want, fix the names and check the regions. A shape without a name is called Imported 1, Imported 2 and so on. The region is guessed from the middle of the shape; when nothing is found, pick one before that shape can be imported. Names follow the same rules as a geofence you draw: up to 50 characters, letters A-Z without accents, digits, spaces and - ' . ( ) &, and not a name you already use or one that appears twice in the file.

The whole file is refused when it isn't .geojson or .json, is larger than 5 MB, isn't valid JSON, or isn't a GeoJSON Feature or FeatureCollection. Within a file that loads:

  • Only Polygon and MultiPolygon shapes are read. Points and lines are skipped and the preview counts them; if nothing else is left, the import stops there.
  • A MultiPolygon keeps only its first shape, because a geofence is one boundary.
  • A shape with fewer than 3 or more than 500 points is flagged and can't be ticked.
  • Only the first 50 shapes are read, and the preview says how many more were left out.
  • Your limit of 10 geofences still applies. The preview warns you when your selection would go past the slots you have left, and the import button is switched off once you're at the limit.
  • A geofence that's saved but couldn't be switched on is listed with the results; flip its toggle to retry.
💡
Reshaping a boundary? Export it, edit the file in a map tool, delete the old geofence here, then import the new one.

Asking for it to go public

If your geofence would help the whole community, send it to the admins for review. Approved, it becomes a public area anyone can select. Your private geofence keeps working while it waits.

The card shows where it stands. A private geofence carries no label. Pending review means it's waiting for an admin. Approved - shared means it's now a public area. Rejected means it wasn't accepted; hover the label to read why. A rejected geofence stays yours and keeps alerting.

ℹ️
You can have up to 10 geofences, each with up to 500 points.
HELP.CONTENT_POKEMON:
A Pokémon alarm tells you when a wild Pokémon spawns that matches your filters.

Adding a Pokémon alarm

  1. Open Pokémon from the sidebar and press New alarm.
  2. Pick the species: type a name or Pokédex number in the search box. Add by type or generation opens the generation and type buttons for browsing, and Add multiple takes a pasted list of names. You can pick several at once.
  3. Set the filters that make a spawn worth hearing about, then save.

The filters you can set:

  • IV between 0 and 100%, CP, and level from 0 to 55.
  • Attack, defence and stamina, each from 0 to 15.
  • Form (Alolan, Galarian and so on), or every form.
  • Gender, weight, and size from XXS to XXL. Leave size on Any to match every size.
  • Time left, under More filters, skips spawns that will be gone before you could get there. The card then shows a pill such as "10 min left".
  • Costume: Any costume ignores costumes, No costume skips costumed spawns, and a named costume matches only that one. Costume names are in English whatever your display language.
ℹ️
The defaults match everything: IV 0-100%, level 0-55, size Any. Change only the filters you care about.

Minior

Minior's IV, CP and level are rolled again for each player who catches it, so a scanner often reports it without them, and a Minior alarm that filters on them never fires. Picking Minior shows a note saying so. Track it with IV, CP and level left open.

PvP filters

Pick a league (Little Cup, Great League or Ultra League) and the rank range you want, say 1 to 50. Level cap chooses the level cap the ranks are read at; leave it on All to use your community's Poracle setting. Mega evolution chooses whether the rule ranks the base form or a mega (Base, Mega, Mega X or Mega Y). Megas are ranked on their own, so a mega rule won't match a base-form spawn.

One alarm for every species

💡
Pick "All Pokémon" to cover every species with one alarm. Pair it with a high IV filter such as 96-100% to catch anything valuable.

Finding an alarm in the list

Search by name, or narrow the list with High IV, PVP or Distance. The generation chips cut the list to one generation, and the sort box orders it by name, Pokédex number, generation or evolution line. When nothing is left on screen, Clear search and filters brings everything back.

Reading the cards

Every alarm list uses the same card: what the rule tracks and its status (such as Clean or Edits in place) at the top, then one line of plain pills for its filters:

IV 90-100%CP 2000+L30-35PVP♂XXL

A coloured edge down the left of a card always means something: a single-species Pokémon card takes its primary type's colour, raid and gym cards their team (grey for any team), and egg cards the colour of their tier's egg. Other cards have no edge.

Most cards also carry Poracle's own one-line description of the rule, which covers details the pills leave out. Press Details, the arrow beside the edit and delete buttons, to read it.

That line is written in your alert language. When it differs from your display language the card leaves the line out rather than mixing two languages. Fort change and Pokéstop event cards never have one.
HELP.CONTENT_OTHER_ALARMS:
Each of these types has its own page that works like the Pokémon one: New alarm at the top, a search box, the count and a sort menu above the cards, and the same card. The sort menu's Default orders cards by what they're titled by, so a card stays put after you edit it.

Raids and eggs

A raid alarm tells you about a raid boss or a hatching egg you want. Raids and eggs have their own tabs on the Raids page.

  • By level tracks every raid of a tier. The chips offer 1 to 4 Star, Legendary, Mega and Mega Legendary, plus Any; More raid types… holds the rest (Ultra Beast, Elite, Primal, the Shadow tiers, Super Mega and Coordinated). Eggs offer 1 to 5 Star.
  • By boss tracks the bosses you pick, at whatever tier they appear.
  • A team filter limits the alarm to gyms held by Mystic, Valor or Instinct.
  • A gym picker limits it to one gym (see below).
  • On By boss you can set a costume the same way as on Pokémon alarms. A by-tier rule and an egg have no costume.

RSVP notifications is covered under Delivery settings.

Max battles

Dynamax and Gigantamax battles at Power Spots.

  • By level tracks any Pokémon at the tiers you pick: 1 to 4 Star, Legendary, Gigantamax and Legendary Gigantamax. Each tier becomes its own alarm, and Select all takes every tier at once.
  • By Pokémon tracks the Pokémon you pick at every tier. Where the site can read the scanner, the picker only offers Pokémon seen in Max battles.
  • Gigantamax only, when tracking by Pokémon, skips everything but Gigantamax battles. By tier, pick the Gigantamax tiers instead.

You can't add the same boss twice at two radii. The second one would replace the first, so it's refused (see the FAQ); change the radius on the alarm you have.

Quests

Field research with a reward you want. Choose the kind of reward in Reward type at the top of the dialog: Pokémon, Items, Mega Energy, Candy, Stardust or PokéCoins.

Items, Mega Energy and candy take a Minimum amount; stardust takes Minimum Stardust and PokéCoins Minimum PokéCoins. Leave it at 0 for any amount. Cards show the amount before the reward, such as "3× Rare Candy".

Invasions

Team GO Rocket at a Pokéstop. Track all invasions makes one alarm for every grunt, leader and Giovanni. Otherwise pick grunt types, leaders or Giovanni, and optionally a gender.

A grunt the bot once saved as "metal" is now called steel, because that's the name the game data uses. A metal rule never matched anything; saved again, it becomes a working steel rule.

Pokéstop events

A DM when a Showcase, Kecleon or Gold Stop appears. Tick one or more when you add the alarm. Each event becomes its own rule, so you can give them different delivery settings later. An event you already track with the same Delivery choice can't be ticked and is marked Already tracked for this Delivery choice. Pick a different Delivery choice to track it there too.

Event cards have no test button and no rule description. On the Profiles page they're listed with your invasion alarms; a profile export includes them, and duplicating or importing a profile carries them over.

If your site or its Poracle server has switched the Pokéstop events page off, it disappears from the sidebar and the three events move to the bottom of the add invasion dialog instead.

Lures

A lure of a given type being placed: Normal, Glacial, Mossy, Magnetic, Rainy or Golden. Ticking several makes one alarm per type.

Nests

A species nesting near you. Set Min spawns/hour so a nest too thin to bother with stays quiet.

Gyms

A gym changing team. Pick the teams to watch (Neutral, Mystic, Valor, Instinct). Track slot changes tells you when a slot opens, and Track battle changes when the gym is under attack.

Fort changes

Changes to Pokéstops and gyms themselves rather than what happens at them: a new one appearing, one removed, or a change to its name, description, location or photo. Choose Pokéstops, gyms or both under Fort type, tick the changes you care about, and turn on Include forts with no name if you want those too.

Targeting one gym

Raid, egg and gym alarms can be limited to a single gym. Type its name into the gym search in the add or edit dialog; the results show each gym's photo, name and area. Once picked, the alarm fires only for that gym and its card names the gym. Leave the field empty, the default, to cover every gym the alarm's delivery reaches. The search only appears where your site can read the scanner.

💡
Mix the two: one raid alarm for every tier at your local gym, and a second for 5-star raids across all your areas.
HELP.CONTENT_DELIVERY:
Every alarm has delivery settings that decide where it reaches you and how the message behaves.

Where an alert reaches you

The Delivery tab of every add and edit dialog asks Where should this alert reach you? and gives three answers:

  • Anywhere in my areas is the default. The alarm follows the areas your profile has selected, so changing your areas changes it too.
  • Near a point sets a radius in kilometres, measured from your pin or from a saved place you choose under Measured from. Without a pin, the picker says so and offers Set your pin. The same list has Add a place, so you can make a place without leaving the dialog.
  • Only in specific areas limits this one alarm to some areas. It offers the areas your profile already has, the geofences you drew, and anything the alarm already points at. It narrows an alarm; it doesn't subscribe you to new areas.

Each alarm answers on its own: areas for Pokémon, a radius from your pin for raids, a named place for quests, if that's what you want.

Under the three answers a small map draws what you picked: the circle around your pin or place, or the areas shaded, including your profile's areas for Anywhere in my areas.

The chip on a card

Most cards carry a chip stating the answer, such as "Anywhere in my areas", "Within 5 km of my pin" or "Within 2 km of Home". It reads "Anywhere I get alerts" when your profile has no areas selected. Click the chip to change that one alarm without opening its edit dialog. On a phone it opens from the bottom of the screen.

Defaults for new alarms

New alarms start on areas. To change that, open the user menu (your avatar, top right), choose Alert defaults, and pick areas or a distance, a default radius, and whether it's measured from your pin or a saved place. The choice is kept in this browser and also fills in the quick pick apply dialog. It affects new alarms only.

When an add or edit is refused

Poracle treats an alarm that differs from one you already have in a single setting (the radius, the template or clean mode) as a change to that alarm, not a new one. Rather than let your new alarm quietly replace the old one, the site refuses it and the dialog stays open with your settings. A line above the buttons names the alarm it clashes with ("Already covered by: …"), and Edit that one opens that alarm instead. An edit that would turn one alarm into a copy of another is refused the same way. When you add several at once, the ones that clash are skipped and the message says why.

Pokémon alarms differ in one case: adding one that matches an existing alarm in everything but clean mode reports it as already tracked and leaves the existing alarm as it was. Edit that alarm to change its clean mode.

Templates

The lower half of the Delivery tab, under Message, decides how the DM behaves. If your site offers templates, you can pick how the message looks. The template selector previews the DM with its layout, fields and images. Preview options under it switches conditions on and off (weather boost, a PvP rank, an EX gym) so you can see how each reads.

Clean mode

With Clean mode on, the bot deletes the alert from your Discord or Telegram DMs once the event is over, for example when a Pokémon despawns or a raid ends. Set it on each alarm, or for a whole type on the Cleaning page. Fort change alarms don't have it.

Editing in place and daily summaries

Edit message in place updates the DM you already have instead of sending a new one. Lures always offer it. Pokémon alarms offer it only when your Poracle server has Pokémon message editing switched on, and then edit only for a short while after the alert was sent. Raids and eggs edit in place by themselves when you pick an RSVP mode.

Daily summary on a quest alarm collects its matches into one message; Quest summary delivery explains when it's sent.

Settings like these that you set through the bot are kept when you edit the alarm here.

RSVP updates (raids and eggs)

RSVP notifications has three choices. Matches only sends the normal alert. Matches + RSVP updates also updates you as trainers sign up. RSVP updates only skips the first alert and tells you only about sign-ups. Either RSVP mode edits the existing DM as the count changes, and the card shows an "RSVP" or "RSVP only" pill.

⚠️
RSVP updates only stays silent unless your community's scanner reports RSVPs. Only pick it if you know it does.

Mention (webhooks only)

While you manage a webhook, the edit dialogs have a Mention field for a Discord role or person to ping when the alert lands in the channel. See Webhooks you manage.
HELP.CONTENT_QUEST_SUMMARY:
Field research changes every day and can match a lot at once, so a broad quest alarm can flood your DMs. A quest summary gathers the matches into one message sent on a schedule.

Two parts

Turn on Daily summary in a quest alarm's dialog to send its matches to the summary instead of alerting at once. Then set a schedule saying when the summary goes out. You need both: the switch says which quests, the schedule says when.

Setting the schedule

On the Quests page, open the ⋮ menu in the toolbar and choose Quest summary delivery. Edit schedule opens the same day and time editor that profile active hours use. Saved times show as amber pills.

The schedule belongs to you, not to a profile, so it's the same on every profile.

Send summary now

Sends whatever has been collected since the last summary, right away. If nothing has been collected yet, nothing is sent.

Good to know

  • The menu only appears when your Poracle server has quest summaries switched on.
  • Your pin sets the time zone. Without one, summaries can arrive at the wrong local time, and the dialog warns you.
  • Removing the schedule leaves the switch on your alarms. Quests still collect, and go out at the bot's default time.
HELP.CONTENT_TEST_ALERTS:
Most alarm cards have a test button (a paper plane) that sends you a sample alert through the bot, built from that alarm's filters and your template. Pokémon, raid, egg, quest, invasion, lure, nest and gym alarms have one. Max battle, fort change and Pokéstop event cards don't, because there's no sample event to build for them.

How it works

Press the paper plane on a card. The site makes up an event that matches the alarm, placed at your pin, and Poracle formats it with your template and sends it to you like a real alert.

Waiting between tests

Each alarm can be tested once every 15 seconds. The button is disabled while you wait, and a message says whether the test was sent, failed, or has to wait.

💡
A test is the quickest way to check a template looks right, or that alerts reach you at all.
HELP.CONTENT_POKEMON_AVAILABILITY:
If your community runs a Golbat scanner, the Pokémon picker shows which species are being seen right now.

The dots

A green dot next to a Pokémon means it has been seen spawning recently. In search results, a faint grey dot means it hasn't; in the tile grid such a Pokémon simply has no dot.

That helps you skip seasonal or event species that aren't around at the moment.

The Spawning filter

Above the picker, the Spawning chip narrows the list to species being reported and tells you how many there are. While any filter is on, available species come first.

The data refreshes by itself in the background.

ℹ️
No dots at all means your community hasn't connected a scanner for this.
HELP.CONTENT_BULK:
Every alarm list lets you change or delete several alarms at once.

Selecting

Press the checklist icon in the toolbar to start selecting. A checkbox appears on each card; tick the ones you want. Clicking elsewhere on a card doesn't select it. Select all ticks everything the search and filters have left on screen, and Deselect all clears the lot.

💡
Select all takes what's on screen, not every alarm of that type. Filter first, then select. Change radius and Delete act only on ticked cards still on screen: a card you ticked and then hid with a search is left alone until you clear the search. On the Raids page they act on the tab in front of you.

Changing the radius

Change radius opens a dialog that says how many alarms you ticked, and only those change. Choose Within a radius and any radius above zero, or Anywhere in my areas for a radius of zero, so the alarms follow your areas. Each alarm keeps what it measures from, your pin or its saved place, and nothing else on it changes.

Each alarm is checked on its own, so one that can't take the change is skipped and the rest go ahead. The message afterwards says how many were skipped and why:

  • An alarm limited to specific areas can't take a radius.
  • An alarm measured from a saved place needs a radius, so it can't be switched to areas this way.
  • An alarm that would clash with another rule is skipped: at the new radius it would match another of your alarms exactly, or so closely that Poracle would merge the two.

Change those alarms one at a time from their chip or edit dialog.

Deleting

Delete removes every ticked alarm after one confirmation.

The Delete button names how many it will remove, and on a phone the bar stays at the bottom of the screen while you scroll.
HELP.CONTENT_QUICK_PICKS:
Quick picks are ready-made alarm sets your admins have put together, such as "100% IV Pokémon" or "All 5-Star Raids". One press creates every alarm in the set.

Applying one

  1. Open Quick picks from the sidebar. The category chips narrow the list.
  2. Press Apply on the one you want.
  3. Adjust it: the Delivery tab is the same three-way choice a single alarm has, so you can aim the set at a saved place or some of your areas. You can also pick a template, turn on clean mode, and leave out particular Pokémon.
  4. Confirm. Every alarm in the set is created at once.

Only alarms that are new are created. One you already have, or one that would replace another of your alarms, is skipped, and the confirmation counts only what was created.

Changing your mind

A pick you have applied shows Re-apply instead of Apply. It reopens the same dialog so you can change the delivery or the exclusions and push them onto the alarms it made. Remove deletes every alarm the pick created.
HELP.CONTENT_PROFILES:
Profiles let you keep separate sets of alarms and switch between them, say "Home" for your neighbourhood and "Work" for around the office. Each profile has its own alarms, areas, pin and geofence switches. Only one is active at a time.

The overview

The Profiles page lists every alarm on every profile. The bar at the top counts alarms by type, the search box looks across all profiles, and the type chips show one kind of alarm at a time.

Each profile is a panel. Open it to see its alarms grouped by type, with sprites and the same filter pills as the alarm lists.

Managing profiles

  • Press New profile at the top right to create a profile.
  • Press Switch in a panel to make it active. The active profile carries an Active badge.
  • The pencil renames a profile.
  • The bin deletes a profile with all its alarms. The active profile can't be deleted.

Names in these dialogs can be up to 32 characters. The create, duplicate and import dialogs warn you as you type a name you already use; renaming checks when you save.

Active hours

Active hours switch a profile on by itself at the times you set. Press the clock icon on a profile to edit them. Tick the days a rule covers (or use Weekdays, Weekends or Every day) and the time the profile switches on.

Repeat until a later time adds an end time and an interval, so "weekdays, 9:00 to 17:00, every 2 hours" is one rule instead of five. A range can't cross midnight. The grid underneath previews the week.

A repeat switches the profile back on at each step rather than holding it for the whole range. If something else takes over at 9:30 (another profile's rule, or you switching by hand), the 11:00 step switches it back.

A profile with no rules never starts by itself; it's only active when you switch to it.

⚠️
Without a pin on the profile, its schedule runs on UTC rather than your local time. The page warns you; set a pin on that profile to fix it.

Duplicating

The copy icon makes a new profile with all of this one's alarms. The name starts as the old one with "(Copy)" added. Areas, pin and active hours are copied too, so the new profile is ready to go.

Export and import

The download icon saves a backup file (JSON) of a profile's alarms. It holds alarms only: no areas, pin or active hours.

Import at the top right reads a backup into a new profile. Alarms already on that profile, or that would replace one there, are skipped. If the name is taken, a number is added, such as "Home (2)".

Duplicates

An alarm that exists more than once, on two profiles or twice on the same one, is marked with a copy tag; hover it to see where the others are. While there are any, a Duplicates chip appears; click it to see only those alarms. Duplicating a profile makes every alarm a duplicate, which is expected.

⚠️
Deleting a profile removes all its alarms for good. Export a backup first if you might want them back.
HELP.CONTENT_CLEANING:
The Cleaning page turns clean mode on or off for a whole alarm type at once. With it on, the bot deletes each alert from your Discord or Telegram DMs once the event is over:

  • Pokémon when they despawn, raids when they end, and eggs when they hatch.
  • Quests at the midnight reset.
  • Invasions when the grunt leaves, and lures when they run out.
  • Nests when they migrate, and Max battles when the battle ends.
  • Gym alerts when the gym changes again.

Pokéstop event alarms aren't on this page, and the Invasions switch leaves them alone even though the two are stored together. Set clean mode on each event alarm in its own dialog. If your site has switched the Pokéstop events page off, the Invasions switch covers them, since nothing else would.

A switch shows as on only when every alarm of that type has clean mode. When only some do, it reads off and a line under it says how many, such as "Clean mode is on for 3 of 5 alarms".

The button at the top reads Enable all, or Disable all once every type is on, and sets every type at once.

💡
Leaving clean mode on keeps old alerts from piling up in your DMs.
HELP.CONTENT_APPEARANCE:
Dark and light

The sun and moon button in the top toolbar switches between dark and light. Your choice is remembered.

Accent colour

Open the user menu (your avatar, top right) and choose Accent theme. It colours the toolbar, the highlighted sidebar item and other accents. Default and Mystic are both blue, Pokémon is green, Instinct is yellow, and Raids and Valor are both red and look almost the same.

Display language

In the user menu, Display language sets the language of this site, including Pokémon names, types and forms in the pickers and on your cards. Until you choose, you get your browser's language, or else the one your Poracle server is set to. Your admin can limit the choice; when only one language is left, the menu item disappears.

Alert language

Just below, Alert language sets the language Poracle writes your DMs in. The two are separate: a German site with English DMs is fine. The alert list only offers languages your Poracle server can write, so it's often the shorter of the two.

Map background

Every map you can work with (the Areas & places map, a geofence's map, the pin picker) has a layers button in its corner. It offers the site's default background, named after the one your admin chose, and the others available. Streets, satellite and plainer styles look very different under an outline, so try a couple.

Your choice applies only to you and only in this browser. If the site's own background can't be drawn, the menu says so and uses one that can.

In dark mode, a map on the site's default background switches to a dark one. Usually that's Esri's dark grey, which zooms in only to level 16; a provider with its own dark style (CARTO, Stadia) uses that instead, and satellite imagery stays as it is. Pick another background from the layers button if you need to zoom closer.

HELP.CONTENT_ALERTS_LOGOUT:
Pausing alerts

Open the user menu (your avatar) and press Pause alerts. A red banner across the top confirms it, and nothing reaches you until you press Resume alerts in the menu or Resume on the banner.

The same banner appears by itself if you keep hitting the DM limit, or if several DMs in a row fail because you've turned off DMs from the server or blocked the bot. Fix the cause, then press Resume. Alerts can take up to 5 minutes to start again.

A second red banner looks similar but says your account is disabled. Resume won't lift that one. It happens when you leave the Discord server or lose a role the site requires; rejoining or getting the role back lifts it by itself. If it doesn't, contact support.

Pausing stops everything until you turn it back on. To silence one gym, area or species for a while instead, use a quiet period (see Quiet periods).

Signing out

Logout in the user menu signs you out and returns you to the login page.

If you signed in through your community's own sign-in and it supports it, the menu also offers Sign out everywhere, which ends that sign-in as well as this site's.
HELP.CONTENT_QUIET:
A quiet period silences one thing for a set time: a gym, an area, a Pokémon species or a Max battle station. Everything else keeps alerting.

Starting one

Look for Quiet on Pokémon, raid, egg, gym, nest and Max battle cards, on the chips of your selected areas, and on each ticked row of the area list. Press it and choose 15 minutes, 30 minutes, 1 hour, 4 hours, 8 hours or 1 day.

It only appears where there's one thing to silence. An alarm for every species, a raid, egg or gym alarm that isn't tied to one gym, and a Max battle alarm without a station have nothing specific to quiet.

Once running, it counts down. Press it again to resume early or to pick a new length. A new length replaces the time left rather than adding to it, so 4 hours means four hours from now.

On the Dashboard

While anything is quiet, a Quiet item joins the status strip on your Dashboard. Click it for the full list, with Resume on each and Resume everything for the lot. Quiet periods you started with the bot are listed too, including ones for a single rule, shown with its type and number such as "raid 60"; you can resume those here as well.

Not the same as pausing

Pause alerts stops every alert until you turn it back on, and puts a red banner across the site. A quiet period is narrow, ends by itself, and shows no banner. If alerts have gone quiet and there's no red banner, look for Quiet on the Dashboard.

Good to know

  • A quiet period can end early, because a Poracle restart clears them all. If alerts come back too soon, start it again.
  • Quiet periods cover your whole account, so switching profile doesn't lift them.
  • If Poracle can't be reached, the site says it couldn't load your quiet periods, and the chips show nothing until it's back.
HELP.CONTENT_WEBHOOKS:
A webhook posts alerts into a Discord channel instead of a DM. It has alarms, areas, profiles and a pin just as you do. An admin can make you a delegate of a webhook so you can look after its alarms without being an admin.

Managing a webhook

Once you're a delegate, My webhooks appears in the sidebar under Webhooks. It lists the webhooks you manage. Press Manage alarms on one and the site switches to that webhook: you see its Dashboard and alarm lists, and anything you add, change or delete is the webhook's. A banner across the top names the webhook; press Back to your account to return to your own.

While you're there you can set up its alarms, areas, profiles and pin, and send test alerts. You can't start or lift quiet periods for it, create or delete webhooks, or add other delegates.

Mentions

A channel alert can ping a role or a person. In an alarm's edit dialog, put a Discord role such as <@&123456789012345678> or a person such as <@123456789012345678> in Mention. Add the alarm first, then edit it, since the add dialogs don't have the field. Pokéstop event alarms don't have it either.

If something's missing

No My webhooks in the sidebar means you haven't been made a delegate yet, or not for a webhook this site knows. A new grant shows up within a minute, and a revoked one goes within a minute too. Managing a webhook here and managing it through the bot on Discord are separate permissions; ask your admins if you need both.
HELP.CONTENT_ADMIN:
The Admin group in the sidebar holds the admin pages. Only admins see this section and those pages.

Users

The people Poracle knows: Discord, Telegram and single sign-on accounts. Channels, groups and webhooks are under Destinations. Search for a person, then open the ⋮ menu on their row to stop or start their alerts, block them, delete all their alarms, or delete the account. Your own row has no block or delete. Deleting an account also removes its geofences, delegate grants and quick picks, and can't be undone.

View shows the site as that person sees it, which is the quickest way to answer "why am I getting nothing?" A banner names the account; Back to your account returns you to yours, on your Dashboard. Changes you make there are made to their account, except quiet periods, which you can see but not change.

Destinations

Where Poracle posts alerts instead of sending them to a person: webhooks, Discord channels and threads, and Telegram channels, groups and topics. Nobody signs in as these, so they aren't listed under Users. Search by name, or filter by type. Add destination takes a name and a Discord webhook URL; a URL that's already in use is refused. Each row can pause, block or delete the webhook, delete its alarms, and open them with Manage alarms. The group icon opens Manage delegates: search for a person (they must have signed in here at least once) and pick them from the list. Locked chips come from Poracle's own config and can't be removed here. A grant takes effect within about a minute. See Webhooks you manage for what a delegate can do. The Delegates column lists only grants actually given, from Poracle's config or this page; admins can manage every webhook, so they aren't listed. For now only webhooks can have delegates.

Areas

Every area Koji serves, with a Hidden switch to take one off the menu without deleting it. A hidden area leaves Areas & places, the per-alarm delivery picker and the bot's own area list. People who already selected it keep it, and keep its alerts, until they remove it themselves. Areas Koji already marks private show as such and can't be changed here. Leaving the page with unsaved changes asks first.

Server settings

Site-wide settings, grouped and searchable, applied as soon as you save. Switches for an alarm type or feature read the positive way round: on means users have it. A type Poracle itself has disabled shows greyed out with a note, because switching it on here couldn't make it work.

A status line under the search sums up two cards and turns amber or red when one needs a look; Details opens them. Versions shows the running PoracleWeb.NET and PoracleNG versions and whether PoracleNG is new enough. If Check for updates is on, it also says whether a newer release exists.

Rule repair finds alarms stored in a shape PoracleNG 5.4.0 reads differently: invasions saved as metal, raids saved with Pokémon 0, and raids or Max battles for any boss saved as Pokémon 9000. Press Scan, check the list, then Repair. Nothing is written until you do, and each alarm is checked again just before it's changed. Alarms PoracleNG won't save at all are listed under Cannot be edited for you to fix by hand or delete.

User geofences

Every geofence your users have drawn. The page opens on the ones waiting for review, oldest first, each with its map, owner, size, region and any public area its centre already falls inside; the rest are in a table below. Review from the row: Approve publishes it as a public area, with a public name and optionally a region, and Reject sends it back with your reason while it stays private for its owner. You can also delete any geofence; if its owner has alarms limited to it, you're asked whether to delete those alarms or keep them on the owner's profile areas.

Quick pick presets

On the Quick picks page, admins get New quick pick at the top and a menu on each pick to edit or delete it. The editor shows only the filters a pick of that alarm type applies: a Pokémon picker (or Any Pokémon), ranges, menus and switches instead of raw numbers, and a grid of icons. Deleting a pick leaves the alarms people created with it. The ⋮ menu at the top offers Reset to defaults, which deletes every admin pick and recreates the built-in set.
HELP.CONTENT_FAQ:
"I can't log in"

Register with the Poracle bot on Discord or Telegram before you sign in here. If you see "Your account is not registered. Please sign up to get started.", look for the Sign up button on the login page, which leads to this site's registration page if it has one. If there's none, contact support.

"I'm not getting notifications"

Work down this list:

  1. Is there a red banner at the top? Your alerts are paused. Press Resume. The banner also turns up by itself after repeated DM limits or failed DMs (DMs from the server switched off, or the bot blocked), so fix that first.
  2. Is something quiet? A quiet period silences a gym, area or species with no banner at all. Look for Quiet in the Dashboard's status strip.
  3. Do you have a pin? An alarm with a radius measures from your pin or a saved place. Set one on the Areas & places page.
  4. Where does the alarm reach you? Read the chip on its card; it may point at areas your profile no longer has.
  5. Are you on the right profile? Your alarms may be on another one. The Dashboard shows which is active.
  6. Are the filters too strict? Loosen IV, CP or level and see whether alerts start.
  7. Is your account disabled? If the site says so, or signs you out as soon as you sign in, Resume won't help. Leaving the Discord server or losing a required role does this, and rejoining or getting the role back lifts it by itself. If it doesn't, contact support.

"A page or option in this guide isn't there"

It has almost certainly been switched off rather than broken. Your admins can switch off any alarm type, Areas & places, Profiles, your pin and places, address search, custom geofences and templates, and Poracle's own configuration can switch off alarm types too, including the Pokéstop events page. A few options follow Poracle's settings: Quest summary delivery needs quest summaries switched on, and Edit message in place on Pokémon alarms needs Pokémon message editing. The availability dots and the gym search need a scanner connected. Ask the team that runs the site if you think something should be on.

Two menus are trimmed on purpose: your admins can limit the display languages, and the alert languages are limited to what your Poracle server can write.

"It says PoracleNG could not be reached"

Your alarms, profiles, pin and areas all live in Poracle, and this site has no copy. When Poracle doesn't answer, pages say the server is temporarily unavailable instead of showing an empty list, and saving fails with "PoracleNG could not be reached. Try again shortly." Nothing is lost. Wait a minute and try again; if it lasts, tell the team that runs the site.

"Another alarm of this type already uses those settings"

Your new or edited alarm differs from one you already have in only one setting (the radius, the template or clean mode). Poracle would treat it as a change to that alarm and replace it, so nothing was saved. Edit the existing alarm, or delete it and add again. Delivery settings explains more. The dialog stays open with your settings, and Edit that one opens the alarm you already have.

"I can't add the same Max battle boss with a second radius"

Same reason: two alarms for one boss that differ only in radius would merge into one, so the second is refused. Change the radius on the alarm you have, or delete it and add the one you want.

"PoracleNG can't store this alarm as it is"

The alarm holds something Poracle can no longer save, usually from an old backup file, an old quick pick, or a rule made through the bot long ago: an egg without a level, an invasion limited to genderless grunts, or a PvP league other than Little Cup, Great League or Ultra League. The message names the field, and nothing was changed. Fix that field in the dialog, or delete the alarm and add it again.

"My metal invasion alarm now says steel"

That's the same grunt. The game data calls it steel, and an alarm saved as metal never matched anything. Saved as steel, it works.

"My alarms disappeared"

Alarms belong to a profile. If you or an active-hours schedule switched profile, the others are still there; switch back from the Dashboard or the Profiles page.

"I can't click a small area on the map"

Zoom in. Smaller areas always sit on top of larger ones.

"What does clean mode do?"

The bot deletes the alert from your Discord or Telegram DMs once the event is over, for example when a Pokémon despawns. Without it, old alerts stay until you delete them. Turn it on per alarm in the Delivery tab, or per type on the Cleaning page.

"Where does an alert reach me?"

Each alarm decides in its Delivery tab. Anywhere in my areas follows your profile's areas, Near a point is a radius from your pin or a saved place, and Only in specific areas keeps that one alarm to some areas. The chip on the card always shows the current answer; click it to change it.

"How do I get rid of test notifications?"

A test sends a real DM through the bot. Once it's sent, this site can't see it or take it back. To clear them, send {{prefix}}poracle-clean to the bot in a direct message and it deletes its own recent messages in that chat. That removes real alerts too, not only tests.

ADMIN_SETTINGS.LOCATION_COMMAND_DESC: The Poracle bot command users run to set their location.
ADMIN_SETTINGS.ENABLE_TELEGRAM_DESC: Allow Telegram login on this site. Requires TELEGRAM_ENABLED=true, bot token, and bot username in .env (server restart required for .env changes).
ADMIN_SETTINGS.TELEGRAM_BOT_DESC: Telegram bot username (without @). Used when TELEGRAM_BOT_USERNAME is not configured.
ADMIN_SETTINGS.ENABLE_DISCORD_DESC: Allow Discord login on this site. Requires Discord Client ID and Client Secret in .env (server restart required for .env changes). Does not affect PoracleNG bot delivery.
ADMIN_SETTINGS.ENABLE_OIDC_DESC: Allow login via the configured external OIDC/OAuth2 provider. Requires OIDC_* settings (provider URLs, client ID, and secret) in .env (server restart required for .env changes).
ADMIN_SETTINGS.AUTH_MODE_LOCAL_DESC: Users sign in with the Discord / Telegram methods configured below.
ADMIN_SETTINGS.AUTH_MODE_OIDC_DESC: All users are redirected to the external SSO provider. Local sign-in is bypassed.
ADMIN_SETTINGS.AUTH_MODE_OIDC_CONFIRM_MSG: After saving, all users (including admins) will be redirected to {{provider}} to sign in — the local Discord/Telegram login page is bypassed. If the provider is unreachable you can be locked out; recover by setting AUTH_FORCE_LOCAL=true in the server environment.
ADMIN_SETTINGS.AUTH_OIDC_NOT_CONFIGURED: SSO is unavailable until the OIDC provider is configured in the server environment (OIDC_* env vars).
ADMIN_SETTINGS.AUTH_OIDC_HIDES_LOCAL: Discord and Telegram are hidden while SSO is the active sign-in mode.
ADMIN_SETTINGS.AUTH_FORCE_LOCAL_ACTIVE: AUTH_FORCE_LOCAL is set in the server environment, so the local login page is being shown regardless of this mode (break-glass override).
ADMIN_SETTINGS.AUTH_SLO_DESC: When enabled, "Sign out everywhere" also ends the provider session (not just this site). Requires the provider's end-session endpoint (OIDC_END_SESSION_URL).
ADMIN_SETTINGS.AUTH_SLO_UNAVAILABLE: Single logout is unavailable until the provider's end-session endpoint is configured (OIDC_END_SESSION_URL env var).
ADMIN_SETTINGS.PROVIDER_URL_DESC: URL template for the map tile provider (used for static maps).
ADMIN_SETTINGS.SIGNUP_URL_DESC: External signup/registration page URL. When set, non-registered users will see a sign-up button on the login page.
ADMIN_SETTINGS.SUPPORT_URL_DESC: Where members go for help: a support channel, a ticket channel or a help page. Linked from the disabled-account banner and the Help page footer. Leave empty to show no link.
ADMIN_SETTINGS.GANALYTICSID_DESC: GA4 measurement ID (leave blank to disable).
ADMIN_SETTINGS.PATREONURL_DESC: Link to your Patreon page shown in the UI.
ADMIN_SETTINGS.PAYPALURL_DESC: Link to your PayPal donation page shown in the UI.
ADMIN_SETTINGS.SITE_IS_HTTPS_DESC: Mark the site as running over HTTPS (affects cookie security).
ADMIN_SETTINGS.DEBUG_DESC: Enable verbose debug logging (not recommended in production).
ADMIN_SETTINGS.TELEGRAM_HINT: Telegram login requires TELEGRAM_ENABLED=true in your .env file along with TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and TELEGRAM_BOT_USERNAME. A server restart is needed after changing .env. The toggle above is an additional on/off switch that takes effect immediately.
ADMIN_SETTINGS.TELEGRAM_ENV_ENABLED_DESC: TELEGRAM_ENABLED value from server config (requires restart to change).
ADMIN_SETTINGS.DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN_DESC: Discord bot token for role verification and notifications (masked).
ADMIN_SETTINGS.DISCORD_GUILD_ID_DESC: Discord server ID for role-based access control.
ADMIN_SETTINGS.DISCORD_ADMIN_IDS_DESC: Discord user IDs with admin access (masked).
ADMIN_SETTINGS.DISCORD_GEOFENCE_FORUM_DESC: Discord forum channel for geofence submission threads.
ADMIN_SETTINGS.LOAD_FAILED: Couldn't load the settings. Reload the page.
ADMIN_SETTINGS.ICONS_SELECTED: Selected {{repo}} icons — click Save to apply
ADMIN_SETTINGS.DISABLE_UPDATE_CHECK_DESC: Lets the site ask GitHub whether a newer PoracleWeb.NET or Poracle has been released. This is the only request it makes outside your own network; nothing is sent with it.
ADMIN_SETTINGS.BASEMAP_PROVIDER_DESC: Which map tiles the site draws by default. The fields below change to match: a built-in provider needs at most an API key, Custom tile URL needs the URL. Viewers can pick a different one from the layers button on any map. In dark mode, viewers on the site default see a provider with no dark style of its own (OpenStreetMap, Esri Streets) as Esri Dark Gray instead, which zooms in to level 16. CARTO and Stadia draw their own dark styles.
ADMIN_SETTINGS.BASEMAP_PROVIDER_UNSET_HINT: No provider chosen, so maps use {{provider}}. Pick one to make it explicit.
ADMIN_SETTINGS.BASEMAP_PERSONAL_OVERRIDE: You are personally viewing {{chosen}}, so this page's setting will not change what you see. The site default is {{provider}}. Pick “Site default” from the layers button on any map to go back to it.
ADMIN_SETTINGS.BASEMAP_KEY_DESC: Key for the chosen provider. It travels in every tile request the browser makes, so it is not a secret — but leaving it blank drops the whole site to a keyless basemap.
ADMIN_SETTINGS.BASEMAP_URL_DESC: Tile URL template for your own provider. Put {key} where it expects the key; {s}, {z}, {x}, {y} and {r} are Leaflet’s.
ADMIN_SETTINGS.BASEMAP_NAME_DESC: What your basemap is called in the layers menu on each map. Leave blank to call it “Custom”.
ADMIN_SETTINGS.BASEMAP_URL_DARK_DESC: Optional. Replaces the tile URL above while a viewer has dark mode on.
ADMIN_SETTINGS.BASEMAP_ATTRIBUTION_DESC: Attribution for the custom tile URL. Must match your provider’s terms. Shown as plain text.
ADMIN_SETTINGS.BASEMAP_KEY_MISSING: No key is set, so maps fall back to {{provider}}. The chosen provider would still return tiles without one — CARTO draws “API KEY REQUIRED” into them — so nothing else would report this.
ADMIN_SETTINGS.BASEMAP_UNAVAILABLE: The chosen basemap has no usable tile URL, so maps fall back to {{provider}}. Pick a provider, or set a Basemap Tile URL starting http:// or https://.
